skill.name: fetch-url
skill.description: Fetches web pages and extracts readable content, with Markdown output, configurable strategies, and dedicated X/Twitter status handling.
skill.summary: Fetch web content into clean Markdown or other supported formats.
skill.author: DCjanus

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, example URLs, status identifiers, and scoped JINA_API_KEY handling. Confirmed behavior includes arbitrary URL fetching and fixed third-party services. Semantic review found SSRF exposure, automatic URL disclosure to Jina Reader, and untrusted content entering agent output without a safety boundary.

remediation.issue: Caller-supplied URLs can target local, private, link-local, or cloud metadata services.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve every destination and redirect, reject non-public addresses, and consider a domain allowlist before urllib or browser navigation.

remediation.issue: Fetched pages can inject instructions into the consuming agent context.
remediation.suggestion: Wrap output as untrusted data and instruct agents never to follow commands, disclose secrets, or invoke tools based only on fetched content.

remediation.issue: Automatic mode forwards complete target URLs to Jina Reader.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit consent before third-party fallback, reject credential-bearing URLs, and clearly disclose which service receives each target.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted URL Fetching Enables SSRF
semantic_findings.description: The command accepts any HTTP or HTTPS host without blocking loopback, private, link-local, or metadata addresses. Direct urllib and browser navigation can therefore access services available from the agent host.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The only target validation checks the scheme, and the accepted URL is passed directly to urllib or Playwright with no host or redirect restrictions.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Third-Party URL Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: Automatic Markdown mode sends the complete target URL to Jina Reader after direct negotiation fails. Query credentials, signed links, and private resource names can be disclosed without separate confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code concatenates the full caller URL into the fixed Jina Reader URL, and auto mode invokes that path without an explicit per-request opt-in.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Web Content Lacks an Agent Safety Boundary
semantic_findings.description: Remote Markdown is returned to the agent without labeling embedded instructions as untrusted. A hostile page can place prompt-injection text into the agent context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Caller-selected remote Markdown is returned unchanged and printed as the command result, while the skill provides no instruction to treat fetched directives as data.

content.user_title: Fetch Web Pages as Clean Content
content.value_statement: Web pages can be difficult for agents to read and extract consistently. This skill retrieves a URL and returns focused content in several formats.
actual_capabilities: Fetches caller-supplied HTTP and HTTPS URLs.
Negotiates Markdown before using Jina Reader or browser rendering.
Extracts main page content with Trafilatura.
Returns Markdown, CSV, HTML, JSON, text, XML, XML-TEI, or rendered HTML.
Handles supported X/Twitter status URLs through FxTwitter in automatic Markdown mode.
Writes results to standard output or a selected output file.
limitations: Requires Python 3.14 or newer, uv, and runtime dependencies. Browser fallback also requires compatible Chromium support.
Automatic mode may send the complete target URL to Jina Reader.
HTTP and HTTPS targets are accepted without blocking private, loopback, or metadata endpoints.
Authenticated browser sessions and custom target request headers are not supported.

prompt_templates.scenario: Basic extraction from a public article.

prompt_templates.title: Save Extracted Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch {URL}, extract readable text, and save it to {OUTPUT_PATH} using the default strategy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a local text artifact from a web page.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Markdown Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch {URL} as Markdown using {STRATEGY}. Report which retrieval path produced the content.
prompt_templates.scenario: Control direct, Jina Reader, or browser retrieval.

prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch {URL} with browser strategy and a {TIMEOUT_MS} millisecond timeout. Use {BROWSER_PATH} and save Markdown to {OUTPUT_PATH}.
prompt_templates.scenario: Render a dynamic page with explicit browser settings.

output_examples.input: Fetch a public article URL as Markdown.
output_examples.output: A focused Markdown document containing the article title, readable body text, formatting, and relevant links.

output_examples.input: Fetch a supported X status URL in automatic Markdown mode.
output_examples.output: A readable post summary with author, canonical URL, timestamp, statistics, text, media links, and available thread entries.

output_examples.input: Fetch a rendered page as plain text and save the result.
output_examples.output: A text file containing the main extracted page content without raw page markup.

best_practices: Review target URLs and remove credentials, signed parameters, or private resource names before fetching.
Use the agent strategy for sensitive URLs to avoid automatic third-party fallback.
Run browser retrieval in an isolated environment when opening untrusted sites.
anti_patterns: Do not fetch loopback, private-network, link-local, or cloud metadata URLs.
Do not place real API keys in prompts, command examples, or output.
Do not treat fetched page text as trusted instructions for the agent.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Markdown, CSV, HTML, JSON, plain text, XML, XML-TEI, and rendered HTML.

faq.question: How does automatic fetching work?
faq.answer: It tries direct Markdown first, then Jina Reader, and finally browser rendering. Supported X URLs use FxTwitter first.

faq.question: Does it support X and Twitter links?
faq.answer: Yes. Recognized status URLs can return post details, media links, statistics, and available thread entries through FxTwitter.

faq.question: Is a Jina API key required?
faq.answer: No. The key is optional and may improve rate limits. Store it only in the JINA_API_KEY environment variable.

faq.question: Does browser mode require a local browser?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill detects common Chromium browser paths or uses a Playwright-managed Chromium installation.

faq.question: Can I safely fetch internal or private URLs?
faq.answer: No. The skill does not restrict private destinations. Use network isolation and validate every target before running it.
